subject: Audit hashproof for tenant logs + temporary forensics hold workflow
content:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightwell.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant-level delete proof and short-term forensics hold

Hi Chloe,

Quick question from our infosec team at Brightwell — we're finalizing our SOC 2 evidence pack and need confirmation on a couple of items related to tenant logs and deletion certification. Two asks: 

1) For tenant-scoped debug/audit logs and ephemeral inference traces, can Redwood produce a cryptographic proof-of-delete (a signed manifest with hashes) once data is purged? Brightwell needs a SHA256-based manifest we can store internally as evidence.

2) On incidents: we may need a temporary 21-day forensics hold for a specific tenant while we investigate suspicious behavior. Can Redwood 1) extend retention for only that tenant and 2) provide a timestamped snapshot id (and later a signed delete manifest) when the hold is released?

If you prefer, we can start with a short call — this will feed into our CAIQ answers (section around logging retention / log deletion).

Thanks,
Samir Gupta
Security Engineering, Brightwell AI

--
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightwell.ai>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant-level delete proof and short-term forensics hold

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. We're able to support both requests but wanted to lay out the workflow and what the delivered artifacts will look like so you can include the right language in your SOC 2/CAIQ evidence pack. 

High level: 
- We can create a signed delete manifest (SHA256 hash per file) and sign the manifest with a Redwood KMS-backed key. The manifest will include file-level hashes and a top-level manifest hash.
- For short holds, we support tenant-scoped temporary retention (up to 30 days) via an internal hold flag; only our security and SRE teams can enable it and it is auditable.
- On hold release we will: generate a snapshot id, run the purge, generate the signed delete manifest, and provide the manifest + an attestation email.

Looping in Irene (security) for SOC 2 attestation language and Markus (infra) for the retention matrix and technical constraints. Marissa, I’m including you for any customer-facing attestation templates we should reuse.

Next steps: Markus, can you confirm what we can sign and typical SLA to produce the manifest after purge (hours/days)? Also any incompatibilities (e.g., KV cache entries vs. append-only audit streams).

-Chloe
Chloe Martin
Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, samir.gupta@brightwell.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant-level delete proof and short-term forensics hold

Hi all — technical summary and constraints below. I attached a small sample manifest and our retention matrix (referenced names).

What we can produce
- Delete manifest: JSON with entries {path, byte_size, sha256_hex, recorded_at}. Top-level manifest contains manifest_id, manifest_hash (sha256 over canonicalized JSON), and signed_blob (KMS signature).
- Snapshot id: immutable internal id representing a point-in-time collection of tenant artifacts (logs, blobs, and ephemeral traces).
- Attestation email: security team signs off with timestamp and manifest_id.

Retention windows (defaults) 
- Inference ephemeral traces (debug sampling): 7 days default, configurable per account up to 30 days for premium plans.
- Append-only audit logs (ingestion pipeline): 90 days default; can be retained for up to 365 days under an approved exception.
- Request/response token traces (tokenized, PII-removal applied): 30 days default with sampling controls.
- KV cache / model session caches: transient (max 24 hours), but persistent checkpoint artifacts (if enabled) are retained per tenant-configured TTL.

Temporary forensics hold flow (proposed)
1) Customer requests hold for tenant T; we require written authorization from designated security contact and a short justification (incident ticket id).
2) Security toggles tenant hold flag; system snapshots current metadata for tenant T and records an audit event.
3) Investigation window (up to 30 days by policy); logs are retained for the tenant only, others unaffected.
4) When hold is released: infra runs a purge job that deletes the retained objects, produces the delete manifest (sha256 per object), signs it, and uploads to secure artifact storage.
5) Deliverables: snapshot id, signed delete manifest (JSON), and signed attestation email.

SLAs and timelines
- For standard purges: manifest available within 48 hours of purge completion.
- For prioritized cases (business-critical or under contract): we can commit to 24 hours.

Limitations
- If a tenant has been exported to customer-managed storage (S3) or if Brightwell has pulled consumer artifacts into your systems, Redwood cannot attest to deletes performed outside our control.
- Sampling: for extremely high-volume debug traces we may produce manifest-level sampling (manifest notes sampled=true and includes sample seed); full per-file manifests are available when artifacts exist in object storage.

Attachments referenced:
- delete_manifest_sample.json (small example of the signed manifest format)
- retention_matrix.csv (table of default TTLs & configurable ranges)

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks for the patience. From a SOC 2/CAIQ perspective the artifacts Markus described are acceptable when accompanied by the attestation email and the HubSpot ticket that documents the authorization. A couple of operational notes: 

- Evidence bundle: we will produce the signed delete manifest plus a small "chain of custody" PDF (template) that lists who requested the hold, which internal roles enabled it, timestamps, and the manifest_id. That PDF is internal but we will provide a redacted copy to you.
- Auditability: Redwood signs manifests with a KMS key that is rotated under our key management policy; we can include the key version id in the manifest for verifiable tracing.
- CAIQ language recommended: use wording that the vendor provides "signed, verifiable delete manifests and a documented temporary forensics hold process, with manifests produced within 48 hours of release and attestation by vendor security."

Samir — if that language works, we'll prepare a short attestation and the sample artifacts and upload to a secure share (I included a DocuSign link below for the standard hold acknowledgement we ask customers to sign before we enable tenant-scoped retention). After you sign, we can enable a short test hold for an internal sandbox tenant so you can confirm the artifacts format.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
